question: What is the cash position and runway?

beats.line: At the end of September, Diginex held one point eight five million dollars in cash.
beats.headline: $1.85M
beats.action: A single halftone stack of paper coins drops onto a cream chip and settles.

beats.line: Six months earlier it was three point one one million — the burn shows a company mid-transition.
beats.headline: $3.11M → $1.85M
beats.action: The stack shrinks coin by coin; a torn-paper arrow slides in and points down.

beats.line: Operating burn ran about one point three million a month.
beats.headline: $1.3M / MONTH
beats.action: The arrow unrolls into a paper calendar strip; coins slide off it month by month.

beats.line: At that rate, the cash on hand covered roughly one point four months.
beats.headline: 1.4 MONTHS
beats.action: The strip becomes a runway that is torn short; a cutout aircraft rolls toward the torn end and stops.

beats.line: An eleven point four million warrant exercise kept the company afloat — and October added thirteen point eight million more.
beats.headline: +$13.8M
beats.action: Fresh paper coins are taped onto the runway one after another, extending it across the frame.

beats.line: Survival depends on capital markets; the next two quarters show whether revenue can narrow the gap.
beats.headline: NEXT 2 QUARTERS
beats.action: Two paper calendar pages land on the runway; a paper hand enters and points at the second.
